teardown.hook: Ranking every major credit card from absolute worst to God-tier, and the number one card quietly draining your cash.
teardown.hook_why: It combines an aggressive superlative tier-list premise with immediate loss aversion, forcing the viewer to watch through to see where their own card lands.

beats.said: Ranking every popular card from trash tier to elite, and the trap card you need to cut up today.
beats.shown: Bold tier list graphic pops up with familiar card logos immediately dragged across tiers.

beats.said: Starting at the bottom: cards charging annual fees with zero real return on everyday spending.
beats.shown: Rapid cut to bottom-tier card breakdown, fee highlighted in bright red text overlay.

beats.said: Mid tier: solid cash back options, but the reward caps eat away half the value if you actually use them.
beats.shown: Quick comparison graphic showing 2% vs 5% category caps with split-screen bar charts.

beats.said: Top tier: the workhorse card that quietly returns real money on every standard dollar spent.
beats.shown: Top tier card sliding into S-rank slot with compounding value counter.

beats.said: Here is how to check your current card lineup against this list before you lose more reward dollars.

teardown.pacing: Rapid-fire 6-to-8 second beat transitions, cutting ruthlessly every 1.5 to 2 seconds visually, maintaining high density of comparative data without downtime across a 30-35 second runtime.
teardown.visual_technique: Tier maker graphic structure with clear color-coded tiers (F to S), instant drag-and-drop animation for items, dynamic on-screen comparison bars, and high-contrast bold captions readable on mute.
reusable_moves: Rapid tier-list hierarchy that instantly categorizes familiar options to trigger debate and high retention.
Early warning hook framing the lowest rank as an active financial leak to drive loss aversion.
teardown.remake_plan: Rank major mega-cap tech stocks or index funds from worst to best performer this week, showing moving stock charts from frame zero to explain which asset protected investor portfolios.
